title: Multiplicity of at least k solutions for the singular critical biharmonic problem with prescribed singularity (Theorem 1.1)
author: Nadjet Yagoub; Mohammed El Mokhtar Ould El Mokhtar; Atika Matallah; Safia Benmansour
work: Multiplicity of solutions for biharmonic equations with critical exponent and prescribed singularity
source_version: Electronic Journal of Differential Equations 2026 (2026), No. 02, pp. 1--15; DOI 10.58997/ejde.2026.02; publisher version
difficulty_reason: The written proof of Theorem 1.1 occupies only lines 1120--1140, and that is exactly the point: it is the top of a source-local chain whose own content is the difficulty. The authors must split the Nehari-type constraint into k localized pieces N_j^- around the k singular poles, prove for each piece that the levels separate as c_{lambda,j} < (2/N) A_mu^{N/4} - chi lambda^2 < hat c_{lambda,j} so that the critical concentration level 2 A_0^{N/4}/N is excluded, and only then may Ekeland's principle be applied to produce a bounded Palais-Smale sequence and, via Lemma 4.2, a strong limit. The distinctness of the k solutions (Remark 3.2) is itself a source-local argument. Concentration-compactness at the critical Sobolev exponent and Ekeland's principle are named prerequisites, but their interaction with the two-sided bounds (1.3) on the multipolar Rellich-type potential V is new and is not reachable by a standard qualifying-exam treatment of fourth-order critical problems.
